'Enforce grammatical rules and call out inefficiencies' is the behavior the passage says readers suspend, and it clashes with 'not immediately ask what do you mean by that?'.

note: Passage is recognizably from Jonathan Culler's discussion of the 'hyper-protected cooperative principle' (Literary Theory: A Very Short Introduction). All five options are grammatically valid in the infinitive slot, so discrimination is purely logical. Option ② is the only candidate consistent with both halves of the passage's characterization of literary reading (effortful interpretation + tolerance of obscurity) and with the coordinated negative clause. Distractors ①/⑤ are polar opposites (attractive to inattentive readers via surface terms like 'communication/efficiency'), ③ is a half-contradiction, ④ is off-topic.
